source: Constructed from DPROD Contracts vocabulary (EKGF dprod, develop, 50db943): dprod-contracts.ttl dprod:not, specification.md §4.9, operands from examples/data-use-policy.ttl and baseline.ttl. No DPROD example uses dprod:not.
notes: Constructed, because no DPROD example uses dprod:not. Rules are named from the start. Operands are declared as in the DPROD examples, with no rdfs:range, so DPROD never raises TypeMismatch for them and comparisons fall through to apply. due2 normalises not(isAnyOf) to isNoneOf and not(and(a, b)) to or(neq a, neq b) (due2-profiles.md §5); these are permission constraints, so the guard/witness split of duty constraints does not arise. DPROD evaluates Not by negating the inner result and propagates errors (formal-semantics.md §6.1, §13.2). DPROD Σ: Σ₀, clock = request.at; there are no duties, so no obligation is ever in force. Scenarios 4 and 5 are DPROD Failures that due2 decides or reports Indeterminate; in scenario 5, De Morgan exposes a false conjunct that makes the U one irrelevant (refinement, not an exception). Scenario 6 is exception 1 under negation: DPROD's apply returns false for the incomparable integer-versus-duration comparison, dprod:not turns that into true, and DPROD grants derive on malformed data, while due2 keeps U through the negation and reports Indeterminate. So 'incomparable is false' is not even fail-safe once dprod:not exists. due2-profiles.md §8.2 exception 1 now states this case: under a prohibition or dprod:not, DPROD's false turns malformed data into a Permit and DPROD fails open, where due2 returns Indeterminate.

scenarios.name: research read of confidential data internally

expected.why: research isNoneOf {marketing, advertising} is T; environment neq external is T, so the De Morgan disjunction is T. rule:neg-read applies. Permit.
marketing isNoneOf {marketing, advertising} is F, so rule:neg-read is F. NotApplicable.

scenarios.name: confidential data to an external environment

expected.why: environment neq external and classification neq confidential are both F, so the negated conjunction is F and rule:neg-read is F. NotApplicable.
The negated purpose atom is U and the second constraint T, so rule:neg-read is U: Permit or NotApplicable depending on the completion.

scenarios.name: environment missing, data public

expected.why: After De Morgan the second constraint is (environment neq external) ∨ (classification neq confidential) = U ∨ T = T; the purpose constraint is T. rule:neg-read applies in every completion. Permit.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Failure(MissingValue ex:environment) (And evaluates the environment conjunct first, inside Not)

scenarios.name: retention period given in the wrong type

expected.why: gt needs operands of the same ordered type; an xsd:integer against an xsd:duration is invalid, so the atom is U, and so is its negation (lteq). rule:neg-derive is U: Permit or NotApplicable.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (apply(gt, 400, P1Y) is false for incomparable operands, §6.2; Not makes it true)

expected.why: P2Y gt P1Y is T (same single component), so its negation is F and rule:neg-derive is F. NotApplicable.
